doc.title: Louis Hayes interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000

title: Joe Zawinul as a bandmate
summary: Zawinul was nervous after accompanying Dinah Washington but worked out wonderfully; Hayes remembers him as a close friend from Vienna.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Yeah. What was he like to work with?

Joe was wonderful. Joe, actually, Joe when he first joined the band Joe was kind of nervous, because he hadn’t been in that situation before. He had been appearing with Dinah Washington, which was — Joe’s facilities were marvelous, but that was a little different accompanying a vocalist naturally. But this was, with Cannonball, it was every person for himself. You had to be ready, creative, you know. Everybody was on their own. So Sam and myself, we used to have these meetings. Because we were so close, you know, friends. So we would have these meetings and sit in the room at night, after the job, and discuss these things. And Joe, he was a little nervous at first, but he worked out just wonderful, worked out just fine.
Oh great, great. And a marvelous, interesting person. You know he’s from Vienna. And him as a person, Joe is a very — we got along so well together. We were very close, good friends.
